title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: How to calculate the total (sum) of a column in a table (Four ways)
summary: The post explains four methods to calculate column totals in Business Central: using AL loops (for, foreach, while, repeat-until), the Record.CalcSums method, Query objects with aggregation, and FlowFields. Each approach has different use cases and performance characteristics for developers calculating sums of data.
key_points: AL loops such as repeat-until work in every situation but are not the most efficient way to total a column
CalcSums totals a field using current filters, is fastest with matching SumIndexFields keys, and does not accept FlowFields
Query objects with the Sum method, optionally grouped by Year, are recommended for frequent calculations at the cost of an extra object
FlowFields defined with CalcFormula show totals on pages without extra code but need a new field in a table

quotes.text: The CalcSums function is used to calculate a total for a specific field, based on the filters of the dataset.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the core purpose and mechanism of the CalcSums method, the most efficient approach for total calculations

quotes.text: This is very useful for displaying totals on a page, as there is no need to add additional logic, just the properties.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights the key advantage of FlowFields: automatic calculation without code, reducing development effort

quotes.text: If frequent calculations are required, this method is recommended.
quotes.why_it_matters: Identifies when Query objects should be used, guiding developers to choose the right approach for their scenario
